reuse.why: Five server sites are routed through the existing getScheduledAmount, but the API's expectedAmount writes its own nested-ternary range resolution instead of calling it.

duplication.why: api-models.ts re-implements the missing/number/range dispatch already in getScheduledAmount, and with the step-1 'furthest from zero' rule rather than the final 'lowest value' rule, so the copy has already diverged.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.getScheduledAmount where amount helpers belong; only the API model computes it locally in the wrong layer.

scope.why: Changes are focused on the amount rule and the API field, with some type churn (Omit<..., 'expectedAmount'>) on create/update handlers to accommodate the field being put on the input type.

maintainability.why: The API field will silently drift from every other path on the next rule change, and the approximate rule only applies where callers remember to pass amountOp (desktop-client callers do not).

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/api-models.ts scheduleModel.toExternal computes expectedAmount inline instead of calling getScheduledAmount.

disguised_duplication.where: api-models.ts expectedAmount: the null/number/range dispatch of getScheduledAmount reshaped as a nested ternary with a Math.abs comparison.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gained an optional amountOp parameter and an 'isapprox' branch inside the number case; scheduleModel.toExternal in api-models.ts bypasses it with its own range logic; desktop-client callers (SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile list) do not pass amountOp.
